title: Schr\"odinger Bridges over Kinetic Swarming Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.25281v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Paradigmatic interaction models explain how collective behaviors can emerge in complex systems from interactions among the constituent agents. In bio-inspired swarms, however, interactions alone may not suffice to bring the population to a desired aggregate configuration within a prescribed time horizon, as needed in applications ranging from targeted therapy to collective transport and emergency evacuation. In the present work, we consider finite-horizon minimum-energy collective steering for inertial swarms that are subject to stochastic disturbances. We focus on the mean-field representations of these multi-agent systems driven by Cucker--Smale alignment or Morse attraction--repulsion interactions. Our objective is to steer the swarm between prescribed endpoint distributions using a state-feedback control, where the endpoint specifications can be full phase-space distributions (positions and velocities) or position marginals alone.

translated_title: 动力学集群模型上的薛定谔桥
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25281v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：典型的交互模型解释了复杂系统中集体行为如何从组成个体之间的相互作用中涌现。然而，在仿生集群中，仅靠相互作用可能不足以在预定时间范围内将群体引导至期望的聚合构型，而这在从靶向治疗到集体运输和紧急疏散等应用中至关重要。在本研究中，我们考虑了受随机扰动影响的惯性集群的有限时间最小能量集体转向问题。我们关注由Cucker--Smale对齐或Morse吸引-排斥相互作用驱动的多智能体系统的平均场表示。我们的目标是使用状态反馈控制，在规定的端点分布（可以是完整的相空间分布（位置和速度）或仅位置边际分布）之间引导集群。
tldr: 本文提出了针对受随机扰动的惯性集群的有限时间最小能量转向方法，利用状态反馈控制实现预定端点分布间的薛定谔桥，并涵盖Cucker-Smale和Morse交互模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a finite-horizon minimum-energy collective steering method for stochastic inertial swarms, using state-feedback control to achieve Schr\"odinger bridges between prescribed endpoint distributions, covering Cucker-Smale and Morse interaction models.
